extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism adjudication bounded to local XML/PDF text and figure captions/images; no direct killing-mechanism overclaim beyond the assays performed in this paper.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: BMAP-27 is framed in the paper as a membranolytic helical peptide that interacts with bacterial membranes; this is background mechanism context used to interpret the EPOL interaction experiments.
mechanism_claims.limitations: The paper does not directly run membrane permeabilization assays for BMAP-27; the statement remains contextual mechanism framing.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Bac7(1-35) is framed as a proline-rich peptide that crosses susceptible bacterial membranes without lysis and targets ribosomes; this explains why its EPOL interaction profile is treated separately from BMAP-27.
mechanism_claims.limitations: The ribosomal targeting mechanism is cited background; this study measures EPOL interaction/protection rather than ribosome binding.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Circular dichroism assays show EPOL-dependent conformational effects: KpTs101/KpTs113 EPOLs induce stronger BMAP-27 alpha-helical structure than KpMn7, while Bac7(1-35) shows smaller CD changes.

mechanism_claims.limitations: CD data support peptide-polysaccharide interaction/conformation but do not by themselves quantify bacterial killing.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: MIC protection assays show EPOLs increase relative MIC against E. coli ML-35, with KpMn7 less protective than KpTs101/KpTs113; this supports polysaccharide-mediated reduction of peptide availability/activity.
